record.paper_title: Structure and dynamics of reentrant nematics: Any open questions after almost 40 years?
record.context_brief: Experimental status of enhanced RN self-diffusivity
record.original_question: Do reentrant nematic phases in single-component, nonpolar molecular liquid crystals exhibit the very large self-diffusivity along the nematic director n that simulations predicted for confined reentrant nematics, and can experiments establish translational diffusion—not another relaxation mechanism—as the cause of the observed dynamical signatures?

evidence.quote: Figure 6 shows a dramatic increase of D∥ as one enters the RN phase whereas lower-pressure (I, N, or SA) phases exhibit rather small self-diffusivity.

However, this remains speculative, until experiments prove that translation diffusion is the main relaxation mechanism at this T. Stronger evidence is found in the conductivity experiments performed by Ratna.
Do RN phases of single-component, nonpolar molecules really exhibit the huge self-diffusivity in the direction of n̂ predicted by our simulations [12, 13]?
At the time of writing some experimental evidence exists suggesting that last question may indeed have a positive answer.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A nematic liquid crystal is a fluid phase of rod-like molecules with long-range orientational order along a unit vector n̂ (the director) but no long-range positional order. A reentrant nematic (RN) phase is a nematic phase that, upon further cooling (or compression) of a given single-component, nonpolar molecular liquid crystal, reappears below an intermediate, more ordered phase such as a smectic-A phase. The self-diffusion tensor of the molecules has principal components D∥ (parallel to n̂) and D⊥ (perpendicular to n̂).

Computer simulations of confined reentrant nematic phases have predicted that, upon entering the RN phase from a higher-temperature smectic or ordinary nematic phase, D∥ increases by roughly an order of magnitude relative to its value in conventional nematic, smectic-A, and isotropic phases at comparable thermodynamic conditions, while D⊥ remains small.

Question: For bulk samples of single-component, nonpolar molecular liquid crystals that exhibit a reentrant nematic phase, do experimental measurements establish:
(a) that the self-diffusivity D∥ along the director is anomalously enhanced in the RN phase by an amount comparable to the simulation prediction (an order-of-magnitude jump relative to the neighboring isotropic, ordinary nematic, and smectic-A phases), and
(b) that this enhancement, together with the associated dynamical signatures observed (e.g., NMR relaxation, conductivity), is genuinely caused by translational self-diffusion of whole molecules along n̂ rather than by some other relaxation mechanism (such as molecular reorientation, collective director fluctuations, or defect-mediated relaxation)?
artifact.status_search_result: The literature shows mixed and partially supportive evidence. Proton NMR work by Miyajima et al. on a pure reentrant nematic compound found Arrhenius behavior dominated by translational diffusion, and a 2012 study reports a diffusivity maximum in a reentrant nematic phase consistent with simulations. However, other experimental measurements of the principal components of the diffusion tensor across nematic, smectic-A, and reentrant nematic phases find that translational dynamics in the RN phase resemble those of the conventional nematic, with no clear order-of-magnitude enhancement. Thus the question is partially settled: enhanced D∥ is supported in some systems, but a definitive demonstration in single-component nonpolar bulk RNs that unambiguously identifies translational diffusion (not other relaxation mechanisms) as the cause is not yet conclusive.

status_evidence.title: Diffusivity Maximum in a Reentrant Nematic Phase
status_evidence.snippet: Diffusivity increases rapidly by an order of magnitude when the reentrant nematic phase forms and then decreases following an Arrhenius law.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental/simulation evidence supports a diffusivity maximum in the RN phase consistent with the simulation prediction.

status_evidence.title: Entropy-Driven Enhanced Self-Diffusion in Confined Reentrant Supernematics
status_evidence.snippet: Supernematic phases exhibit a remarkably high self-diffusivity along the director, exceeding ordinary nematics by an order of magnitude.
status_evidence.claim: Original simulation prediction of enhanced D∥ in confined reentrant supernematics.

status_evidence.title: Anisotropic self-diffusion in nematic, smectic-A, and reentrant nematic phases
status_evidence.snippet: The principal components of the diffusion tensor have been determined and compared across phases; results suggest similarity of conventional and reentrant nematic translational dynamics in some systems.
status_evidence.claim: Some experiments do not see a clear order-of-magnitude enhancement, leaving the issue partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Phase Transitions and Dynamics in Reentrant Nematic Liquid Crystals by Xe-129 NMR
status_evidence.snippet: NMR characterization of dynamics in reentrant nematic liquid crystals.
status_evidence.claim: NMR-based experimental probes provide partial evidence regarding translational vs. other relaxation mechanisms.
